title: The Judge with the Iron Balance (MR)
summary: A provincial judge favors his own relatives in a property dispute. Birbal presents an iron balance that tilts only toward gold. [MR]
full_text:
Complaints reached Emperor Akbar that the chief Qazi of Lahore was notoriously corrupt, consistently ruling in favor of his own wealthy relatives in property disputes, regardless of evidence.

When questioned by Akbar, the Qazi swore solemnly: 'Your Majesty, my judicial balance is as straight and incorruptible as iron! I judge solely by truth!'

Akbar sent Birbal to Lahore to investigate.

Birbal arrived at the court of Lahore, carrying a handsome iron balance beam used for weighing silver and gold. Birbal presented it as an imperial gift to the Qazi.

The Qazi examined the balance: 'A magnificent set of scales, Lord Birbal! Perfectly balanced!'

Birbal said: 'Let us test its precision. Place an equal weight of lead on both pans.'

When equal lead weights were placed, the right pan sank heavily, while the left pan rose into the air!

The Qazi frowned: 'The scales are defective! The right pan sinks even though the weights are equal!'

Birbal stepped forward and tapped the right arm of the balance with a small hammer. A hidden cavity inside the iron arm opened, revealing a heavy lump of magnet embedded within the metal!

Birbal looked into the Qazi's eyes with razor-sharp solemnity:

'Just so, noble Qazi! On the outside, this balance appears to be made of righteous iron. But on the inside, a hidden magnet pulls the pan down, ensuring that one side always wins!

'Your court in Lahore is identical to this fraudulent balance! On the outside, you proclaim the majesty of the law. But on the inside, the hidden magnet of family favoritism and bribes tilts your judgments, robbing the innocent and crushing the poor!

'A judge who holds a magnetic balance destroys the sacred covenant of justice!'

The Qazi turned pale, fell to his knees, and confessed his corrupt rulings. Birbal stripped him of his robes, reversed the unjust property judgments, and appointed an honest magistrate in his place.

Akbar praised Birbal for exposing corruption with an unforgettable visual parable.
